section_headings: What are the genetics of Piescream?

article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Indica-leaning hybrid
Genetics: Wedding Pie × Gelato #33 × Cherry Limeade F5
Breeder: Freeborn Selections by Mean Gene, in collaboration with Skunktek
THC Content: 25-28%
CBD Content: Typically below 1%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , caryophyllene , pinene
Primary Flavors: Sweet cream, cherry, lime, berry pastry
Flowering Time (Indoor): 8–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: early to mid-October
Indoor Yield: Moderate
Outdoor Yield: Moderate to high
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Piescream is a dessert strain in name, but its aroma is considerably stranger and more aggressive than the label suggests. Sweet berry pastry and creamy vanilla can appear immediately when the jar opens, yet those softer notes quickly mix with sour cream, lime, gasoline, skunk, and an almost cooling menthol quality. Some flowers push toward sugared cherries dipped in fuel; others lean into creamy sherbet, tart citrus, or dough. Freeborn Selections describes particularly good examples as intensely resinous, with a greasy texture that goes beyond ordinary sticky cannabis and leaves an oily residue before drying on the fingers.

The cultivar was created by Mean Gene of Freeborn Selections using a Wedding Pie female selected by Skunktek from Cannarado genetics. That female was crossed to a Freeborn line combining Gelato #33 with Cherry Limeade F5. Freeborn’s own documentation identifies Wedding Pie as Wedding Cake × Grape Pie , while the Gelato #33 side contributes Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint GSC ancestry. Piescream therefore brings together grape pastry, Cookies, sherbet, lime, cherry, skunk, and gas genetics in one unusually resinous hybrid.
Genetics and Lineage

Wedding Pie forms the maternal foundation and supplies much of the dense dessert character. Created from Wedding Cake and Grape Pie, it brings sweet dough, grape fruitiness, cream, and substantial resin production. Wedding Cake adds the vanilla-frosting and earthy Cookies side of the pedigree, while Grape Pie contributes darker fruit, pastry, and floral depth. Skunktek’s selection of the Wedding Pie female became particularly important because Piescream’s reputation is closely tied to the quality of that chosen parent rather than Wedding Pie genetics in the abstract.

The paternal side is Gelato #33 × Cherry Limeade F5. Gelato #33 supplies cream, sweet fruit, flowers, and gas through its Sunset Sherbet and Thin Mint GSC ancestry. Cherry Limeade pushes the profile into brighter territory with tart cherry, citrus, lime, and pungent funk. Freeborn’s F5 work on the Cherry Limeade side also gives this half of the pedigree considerably more breeding depth than a simple first-generation fruit cross.

Bringing those families together explains Piescream’s unusually broad aromatic range. Wedding Pie anchors the cultivar with grape, baked goods, and dense sweetness; Gelato #33 adds creamy dessert terpenes; Cherry Limeade brings acidity and sharp fruit. Skunk and fuel emerge underneath all three. 710 Labs summarizes its selected Piescream expression with sweet, menthol, and cream flavor tags and describes the profile as sweet sherbet coated with menthol and sour cream.
Effects and Experience

Piescream often begins more brightly than its indica-leaning reputation suggests. The early phase can bring noticeable euphoria, an improved mood, and a relaxed but socially engaged frame of mind. Conversation may become easier, humor feels more immediate, and music or visual entertainment can become particularly immersive. Rather than instantly slowing thought, moderate amounts often preserve enough mental energy for creative or social activity.

The physical side develops more gradually. Tension through the shoulders and limbs can soften while the initial cerebral lift settles into a warmer, heavier state. Proper Cannabis describes its Piescream #27 as uplifting and giggly at first, followed by relaxing physical comfort and increased appetite. Its tested expression is led by beta-myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and alpha-pinene. That combination fits the cultivar’s reputation for simultaneously producing mental uplift and substantial physical calm.

Dose strongly influences the final result. Contemporary commercial flower has appeared close to 29% THC and higher, so inexperienced consumers should not assume that the creamy flavor indicates mild potency. Stronger consumption can produce heavy eyelids, slowed concentration, hunger, and a much more stationary experience. Dry mouth, dry eyes, dizziness, or anxiety can occur when THC intake exceeds personal tolerance.
Medical Benefits

Piescream has not been studied in controlled clinical trials as an individual medical marijuana cultivar, so claims that it treats specific conditions would be unsupported. Its combination of euphoria and progressive relaxation may nevertheless explain why some medical cannabis consumers gravitate toward similar THC-dominant hybrids for temporary relief from stress, poor appetite, minor discomfort, or difficulty settling down.

The cultivar may have particular appeal for people who prefer an initial mental lift before stronger body relaxation arrives. At moderate doses, that progression can feel less immediately sedating than a traditional heavy indica. Higher amounts, however, can interfere with attention, coordination, and short-term memory and may become substantially more sedating.

Terpene content varies between commercial selections. The Pass lists myrcene, ocimene, pinene, and caryophyllene for its Piescream flower, while Proper Cannabis identifies beta-myrcene, beta-caryophyllene, and alpha-pinene in Piescream #27. Those differences reinforce why medical consumers should rely on the certificate of analysis for their specific batch instead of assuming one universal chemical profile.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Dessert sweetness leads, but Piescream earns much of its reputation from what follows. Fresh flowers can release ripe berries, cherry pastry, vanilla cream, and sugary dough before sour citrus and skunk begin cutting through. Freeborn describes Piescream #27 as smelling like sugared cherries dipped in gas and tasting like a doughy berry streusel. That description captures the cultivar better than simply calling it sweet.

Grinding the flower generally exposes the sharper side of the genetics. Lime zest, sour cream, fuel, and herbal skunk can become much stronger, while the creamy fruit remains in the background. Certain selections develop a cooling menthol sensation that contrasts sharply with the pastry sweetness. 710 Labs’ hunted cut emphasizes precisely that combination, pairing sherbet-like sweetness with menthol and a puckering sour-cream finish.

The inhale tends to begin with cream, berries, and sweet dough. Cherry and tart lime appear through the middle, followed by gasoline and skunk on the exhale. Some phenotypes lean toward grape pie, while others become more cherry-lime dominant. High resin concentration can make the flavor unusually persistent, which helps explain why Piescream has also become sought after for hash and rosin production.
Growing Information

Freeborn Selections still offers Piescream as regular seed but does not publish a rigid flowering-time or yield specification for the cultivar. The breeder instead emphasizes that yield depends heavily on plant variety, conditions, farming practices, and weather. Cultivation references generally place the flowering window around eight to ten weeks, but growers should treat that as an approximate range and judge individual plants by flower and trichome maturity.

Resin production is arguably the cultivar’s most important cultivation trait. The best-known selections can become exceptionally greasy late in flower, with dense trichome coverage extending across violet and green buds. Good airflow becomes increasingly important as flowers gain weight and resin, particularly where canopies are tightly packed. Strategic pruning before flowering can improve interior light penetration and help reduce stagnant humidity around lower bud sites.

Phenotype hunting is especially relevant with Piescream. Skunktek’s famous #27 selection came from a seed hunt, and Freeborn specifically notes that the number refers to the 27th plant selected from the population. A grower working through authentic regular seed should therefore expect meaningful differences in fruit balance, resin texture, structure, and potency. Keeper selection can reasonably prioritize resin production, cherry-lime intensity, creamy gas, flower density, and resistance to late-flower stress rather than yield alone.

Outdoor plants should receive ample sunlight and enough season length to finish properly. In climates with wet autumns, flower density and heavy resin make moisture management important approaching harvest. Slow drying at controlled temperatures is equally valuable after harvest because much of the cultivar’s character depends on volatile cherry, lime, cream, and menthol compounds that can disappear under excessive heat.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Piescream?

Piescream is Wedding Pie × (Gelato #33 × Cherry Limeade F5). Freeborn Selections documents Wedding Pie as Wedding Cake × Grape Pie and identifies the second parent as a Gelato #33 and Cherry Limeade F5 combination.
Who bred the Piescream strain?

Piescream was bred by Mean Gene of Freeborn Selections in collaboration with Skunktek. Skunktek selected the Wedding Pie female used in the cross and later hunted notable Piescream phenotypes, including Piescream #27.
Is Piescream indica or sativa?
It is best described as an indica-leaning hybrid. Its effects often begin with euphoric, social, and creative energy before stronger body relaxation and heaviness develop.
What does Piescream taste like?

Expect sweet cream, cherry, berry pastry, vanilla, sour lime, gas, skunk, and sometimes menthol. Some selections lean toward grape pie and dough, while others emphasize tart cherry-lime and sour cream.
How strong is Piescream weed?

Commercial flower frequently reaches the upper-20% THC range, although potency varies by grower and phenotype. One current Sense-grown product is listed at 28.8% THC. Consumers should always use the laboratory result from their specific batch rather than assuming one fixed strain percentage.
Final Thoughts on Piescream

Piescream is a strong example of dessert cannabis that refuses to stay entirely sweet. Wedding Pie gives the cultivar grape pastry, dough, and resin; Gelato #33 brings cream and sherbet; Cherry Limeade F5 cuts through both with tart fruit, citrus, and funk. Gas, skunk, and menthol underneath those flavors keep the flower interesting after the initial dessert impression fades.

Its resin production may be just as important as its flavor. Freeborn’s documentation of unusually greasy flower, combined with the cultivar’s adoption by 710 Labs and solventless producers, shows why Piescream has developed a reputation beyond ordinary premium flower. The #27 selection in particular demonstrates how much quality can emerge from careful phenotype hunting within the original seed population.

For cannabis enthusiasts who enjoy Wedding Cake, Gelato, Grape Pie, and cherry-lime genetics but want something more distinctive than another sweet hybrid, Piescream offers an unusually complete profile. Cream and berries make the first impression approachable; sour lime, fuel, skunk, menthol, and strong physical relaxation provide the depth. That combination of dessert flavor, greasy resin, potent effects, and legitimate breeder provenance has made Piescream one of Freeborn Selections’ most recognizable modern marijuana strains .
